findings.problem: Remove duplicate primary key entries for `product_id` in `products`
findings.fix: Duplicate primary key values violate data integrity. This fix removes duplicate rows, keeping one arbitrary record for each `product_id`, and then adds a unique constraint to prevent future duplicates. Deleted rows cannot be rolled back.
queries:
DELETE FROM products
WHERE product_id IN (
    SELECT product_id
    FROM products
    GROUP BY product_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
) AND ctid NOT IN (
    SELECT MIN(ctid)
    FROM products
    GROUP BY product_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
);
ALTER TABLE products ADD CONSTRAINT products_product_id_unique UNIQUE (product_id);
findings.explanation: Duplicate primary key values violate data integrity. This fix removes duplicate rows, keeping one arbitrary record for each `product_id`, and then adds a unique constraint to prevent future duplicates. Deleted rows cannot be rolled back.
verification_queries: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products GROUP BY product_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
rollback_queries: ALTER TABLE products DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS products_product_id_unique;
